checked_ok.claim: TestFlight allows up to 10,000 external testers, and the first build added to a group is sent to App Review (later builds may not need a full review).
Each TestFlight build is testable for up to 90 days from the day it is uploaded.
The App Review demo account must not expire.

DPLA 7.4(B) (agreement last updated 2026-08-18): external TestFlight is 'solely for their testing and evaluation of such pre-release versions', and 'continuous distribution of demo versions of Your Application in an attempt to circumvent the App Store' is a prohibited use. So TestFlight cannot be the permanent channel.
Unlisted apps are reachable only by direct link and do not appear in search. Apple names 'higher-education students' as a fitting limited audience.

Unlisted needs a final version submitted to App Review, and requests for beta or prerelease apps are declined. The request is a Review Notes entry plus the request form. Once approved, the method switches to Unlisted for all future versions, which then ship through the normal App Store process with no 90-day expiry.

Unlisted is the right choice over a public listing. App Review rejects public distribution of apps 'intended to be used by a specific business or organization' under guideline 3.2 (rejection text quoted on Apple's forum, May 2025).

Apple asks unlisted apps to block unauthorized use ('Consider implementing a mechanism within your app to prevent unauthorized use'). The plan's student-list matching and device binding already do this.

Guideline 5.2.1 requires permission for protected third-party marks and says apps should be submitted by the owner or licensee of the rights. Guideline 4.1(c) also bars using another developer's brand in an app's icon or name without approval, and an İÜ unit (AUZEF) already publishes on the App Store under its own developer name.

The annual fee is 99 USD (or local currency). The fee waiver is only for legal entities (nonprofits, accredited educational institutions, government) and explicitly excludes 'an individual, sole proprietor, or single-person business'.
Free sideloading still expires every 7 days: 'Apps installed with AltStore expire after 7 days', and there is a 3-app limit. Apple's free Personal Team profiles also expire 7 days from issuance.
Apple's alternative app distribution exists only in Brazil, Japan and the EU (page dated 2026-06-18), so nothing changes the 7-day limit for users in Türkiye.

xprem is real: it is the renamed expo-open-ota, and the plan's Kaynaklar link redirects to it. It implements the official Expo Updates protocol with Expo's own expo-updates client, and its MIT core includes publishing, rollbacks, progressive rollouts, the dashboard and code signing. It is active (v3.2.5 on 2026-09-26; eoas CLI about 19.7k weekly downloads) and owned by an organization (Mercure Technologies), but one author made about 514 of the commits.

'Only bug fixes, no new features over OTA' matches Apple's rules. Guideline 2.5.2 bans downloaded code 'which introduces or changes features or functionality'. DPLA 3.3.1(B) allows interpreted code only if it does not change the primary purpose, and 3.3.1(C) bans unlocking 'additional features or functionality' outside the App Store, Custom App Distribution or TestFlight.
Putting the OTA setup in the first release is required, because the update server URL and the signing certificate are embedded at build time.
The same OTA rule also passes Google Play if the Play closed test is added. Play's self-update ban 'does not apply to code that runs in a virtual machine or an interpreter' such as JavaScript.

GitHub limits unauthenticated REST requests to 60 per hour, counted per originating IP address. Phones behind one shared campus IP would exhaust it, so routing through the plan's own server is correct.

Staged rollout needs no extra tool. App Store phased release spreads an update over 7 days (1% up to 100%) and can be paused for up to 30 days. xprem control-plane mode gives percentage rollouts for OTA updates.

expo-updates is current: latest 57.0.24 on the sdk-57 tag (npm, modified 2026-10-03). Expo Updates protocol v1 supports signed manifests (rsa-v1_5-sha256) and the rollBackToEmbedded directive (spec modified 2026-08-12).
xprem handles the plan's peak. Its manifest endpoint held p95 1.39 ms at 650 req/s on 1 vCPU, and bundle bytes are served by object storage, not by the server process.
The order 'TestFlight first, then unlisted App Store' matches Apple, which declines unlisted requests for apps in a beta or prerelease state.

findings.plan_quote: TestFlight: en çok 10.000 kişi, her derleme 90 gün.
findings.finding: A TestFlight build stops opening 90 days after upload, and an OTA update does not extend the binary's life. A pilot semester is longer than 90 days, so at least one new TestFlight build must be installed mid-semester. That contradicts line 513 ('Dönem ortasında zorunlu güncelleme ... yok') for the TestFlight phase. Once a build has expired the app cannot open, so unsent records cannot be sent until the student installs the new build.

evidence.quote: Each build is available to test for up to 90 days, starting from the day the developer uploads their build.
When the testing period is over, you'll no longer be able to open the beta build.
With TestFlight 3 or later, you can turn on automatic updates to have the latest beta builds install automatically.

findings.recommendation_tr: Deneme döneminde her TestFlight derlemesi yüklendiği günden 90 gün sonra açılmaz olur; uzaktan güncelleme bu süreyi uzatmaz. Süre dolmadan yeni derleme yüklerim ve öğrencilerden TestFlight'ta otomatik güncellemeyi açmalarını isterim. 'Dönem ortasında zorunlu güncelleme yok' kuralına deneme dönemi için bu tek istisnayı yazarım.

findings.plan_quote: uygulamada deneme hesabı ve her an açık deneme dersi bulunur
findings.finding: Apple needs a working demo account that never expires, for every TestFlight external review and for every App Store version. Four of the plan's own rules would stop a reviewer. Instructor login is email-code only (line 69). Release builds have no 'show code' option (line 87). Instructor accounts wait for admin approval (line 66). A student account is bound to one phone, and changing phones needs a face-to-face approval (line 84). Reviewers cannot open the demo mailbox, and each review may run on a different device. The demo accounts have to be designed around these rules, and the back end must stay reachable from outside Türkiye during review.

evidence.quote: include demo account info (and turn on your back-end service!) if your app includes a login. If you are unable to provide a demo account due to legal or security obligations, you may include a built-in demo mode in lieu of a demo account with prior approval by Apple.
The demo account is used during the App Review process and must not expire.
the reviewer do not have access to the email inbox or phone number of that demo account

findings.recommendation_tr: İnceleme için önceden onaylı bir deneme hocası ve bir deneme öğrencisi kurarım. Deneme hocası e-postaya gelen kod yerine yalnız bu hesaba tanımlı sabit bir kodla girer. Deneme öğrencisi tek telefon kuralından muaftır, her incelemede başka bir cihazdan girebilir. Bu iki hesap yalnız deneme dersini görür ve her girişleri kayda geçer. Sunucu inceleme sırasında yurt dışından da erişilebilir kalır.

findings.plan_quote: Bireysel hesabın bunu kullanıp kullanamayacağı doğrulanmadı.
findings.finding: The plan leaves the Apple account owner open, but changing it after launch is costly. Transferring an app to another team breaks keychain access tied to the App ID prefix. This plan keeps each student's device-bound key on the phone, so after a transfer every iPhone student could have to redo the face-to-face device change. Apple's unlisted page names no account-type condition, so an individual account can apply, and approval is at Apple's discretion. The fee waiver is only for legal entities such as accredited educational institutions, never individuals. An İÜ unit (AUZEF) already has an App Store organization account, which matters for both the waiver and the name and logo permission.

evidence.quote: After the update, users must re-login once as the app cannot retrieve the authentication token from the keychain.
Keychain access groups from the first two bullets depend on the App ID prefix. If that changes, you lose access to any keychain items in those groups.
Not be an individual, sole proprietor, or single-person business;
İstanbul Üniversitesi Açık ve Uzaktan Eğitim Fakültesi (developer and seller name)

findings.recommendation_tr: Uygulamayı hangi Apple hesabıyla yayınlayacağımı ilk TestFlight derlemesinden önce kesinleştiririm ve sonra değiştirmem; iş sırasındaki dağıtım adımı bu kararla başlar. Uygulama sonradan başka hesaba aktarılırsa telefonda saklanan anahtarlara erişim kopabilir ve iPhone kullanan her öğrenci cihaz değişimi akışından geçer. Apple'ın listelenmeyen dağıtım sayfası hesap türü için sınır koymuyor; bireysel hesabımla başvururum. İÜ'nün kurum hesabı kullanılacaksa (AUZEF bu hesapla App Store'da) ücret muafiyeti istenebilir ve ad ile logo izni kolaylaşır; bu seçenek de aynı kararda konuşulur.

findings.plan_quote: kendi sunucumdaki güncelleme servisiyle (xprem, Expo Updates protokolü) güncellenir
findings.finding: The plan does not say which xprem mode it runs, and the modes differ in what the plan needs. Stateless mode needs an Expo access token and rejects rollout percentages. Rollouts need control-plane mode with PostgreSQL and a master key; in v3 that mode publishes without any Expo account. Production storage is also missing from the plan. xprem says its local-disk storage is not recommended for production, and the usual self-hosted S3 server, MinIO, was archived in April 2026. The update URL is baked into every build, so it should sit on a domain the owner controls. The plan's Kaynaklar link still uses the old repo name.

evidence.quote: Progressive rollouts: `--rollout-percentage` is rejected with an explicit error
Progressive rollouts require a control-plane server: rollout state lives in Postgres. They are part of the open-source core, so no Enterprise license is needed.
This storage solution is not recommended for production use.
"archived": true, "pushed_at": "2026-04-24T17:54:39Z"
The server URL and signing certificate are embedded at build time, so any build made before this change will keep pointing at the old configuration.

findings.recommendation_tr: xprem'i 'control plane' modunda çalıştırırım. Kademeli açma yalnız bu modda var, durumunu PostgreSQL'de tutuyor ve Expo hesabı istemiyor. Mevcut PostgreSQL sunucumda ayrı bir xprem veritabanı açarım; Redis ve CDN eklemem. Güncelleme dosyalarını yerel disk yerine S3 uyumlu bir depolama kovasında tutarım, çünkü xprem yerel diski üretim için önermiyor. MinIO'yu kendim kurmam, Nisan 2026'da arşivlendi. Güncelleme adresi baştan kendi alan adımda olur; adres derlemeye gömüldüğü için sunucu değişse de uygulamayı yeniden derlemem gerekmez. xprem imajını sürüm etiketiyle sabitlerim, kaynaklardaki bağlantıyı github.com/mercuretechnologies/xprem yaparım.

findings.plan_quote: expo-updates, kendi sunucumdaki xprem ile; güncellemeler imzalı.
findings.finding: xprem signs manifests itself. The private key is generated on the server, kept in PostgreSQL and unlocked by a master key that cannot be recovered. This has two consequences. First, the signature does not protect against anyone who reaches the xprem dashboard or a publish token: they can push signed JavaScript to every phone and undermine attendance integrity. IP allowlisting and SSO are Enterprise-only, and in the MIT core the dashboard has password login on the same host as the public manifest endpoint. Second, if the master key is lost and no offline copy of the signing key exists, installed apps reject every future update until everyone installs a new binary. Line 519's offline backup of the 'güncelleme imza anahtarı' therefore only works if the key is generated outside xprem first.

evidence.quote: It generates an RSA pair when the app is created and seals it in PostgreSQL with the master key.
The master key is not recoverable, so back it up before your first deployment.
the server reads your local or environment keys once and seals them into the database with the master key.
Token access rules, which scope an API key to the branches whose names match the patterns you give it, and restrict where it may be used from with an IP allowlist
The server then renders the dashboard at `/dashboard`.

findings.recommendation_tr: xprem güncellemeleri kendi sunucusunda tuttuğu anahtarla imzalıyor. Bu yüzden imza, sunucuya ya da yayın anahtarına erişen birine karşı korumaz. İmza anahtarını kendim üretirim (eoas generate-certs), çevrimdışı yedeklerim ve xprem'e ilk açılışta öyle veririm. xprem'in ana anahtarı da çevrimdışı yedek listesine girer. xprem paneli internete açılmaz, yalnız SSH tüneliyle açılır; yayın anahtarı yalnız CI'da durur.

findings.plan_quote: Yerel kod değişikliği ve yeni özellik yeni sürümle gelir.
findings.finding: The plan does not say how an OTA update is kept away from binaries whose native code differs; in Expo the runtimeVersion policy does this. The app has its own native module, so an incompatible JavaScript update could call code missing from older builds. xprem recommends a fixed runtimeVersion that is bumped before every native-changing build. It warns against the fingerprint policy, because CI and local machines can compute different values and the update then silently never arrives.

evidence.quote: Bump it before every build that changes native code. This includes native dependencies, config plugins, and files under `ios/` or `android/`.
CI and local environments can produce different fingerprints for one commit. The only symptom is an update that never arrives.
If the update would make calls to code that does not exist inside the build, `expo-updates` may detect an error and attempt to roll back to the previously working update.

findings.recommendation_tr: Uzaktan güncellemenin yalnız uyumlu derlemeye gitmesi için runtimeVersion'ı elle yazılan sabit bir değer olarak tutarım. Yerel kodu değiştiren her derlemeden önce bu değeri artırırım: yerel modül, yapılandırma eklentisi, ios ve android klasörleri. Fingerprint kuralını kullanmam; CI ile kendi bilgisayarım farklı değer üretirse güncelleme sessizce hiç gelmez.

findings.plan_quote: Güncellemeler imzalıdır, kademeli açılır ve geri alınabilir.
findings.finding: Rollback in xprem returns phones to the update embedded in the binary. Expo warns that an update may already have changed persistent data in a non-backwards-compatible way. If an OTA update ships a change to the local expo-sqlite schema of the send queue, a rollback runs older code against the newer schema. That puts unsent records at risk and conflicts with the 'Kayıt kaybı 0' target.

evidence.quote: your broken update may, for example, have modified persistent state (such as data stored in AsyncStorage or on the device's file system) in a non-backwards-compatible way.
A rollback update reverts the application on the specified branch to the embedded update without requiring a new native build.

findings.recommendation_tr: Telefondaki yerel veritabanının yapısını uzaktan güncellemeyle değiştirmem; yapı değişikliği yalnız yeni APK ya da App Store sürümüyle gelir. Böylece bir güncelleme geri alındığında eski kod yeni yapılı bir veritabanıyla karşılaşmaz ve bekleyen kayıtlar okunur kalır.

findings.plan_quote: Uygulama açılışta, günde en çok bir kez kendi sunucuma sorar.
findings.finding: Requests carry only the app version, but with OTA the version alone no longer tells which JavaScript produced a record. expo-updates exposes the running update's UUID. Sending it in the version check and with each upload costs nothing. It lets the server tie bad records or crashes to one update and decide a rollback on data.

evidence.quote: The UUID that uniquely identifies the currently running update.

findings.recommendation_tr: Telefon, sürüm kontrolünde ve her gönderimde uygulama sürümüyle birlikte çalışan uzaktan güncellemenin kimliğini (updateId) de bildirir. Hatalı bir güncellemenin hangi kayıtları etkilediği sunucuda görünür ve geri alma kararı veriye dayanır.

findings.plan_quote: ya da GitHub'dan anahtarla ve önbellekle okur; APK'nın özet değerini ve izin verilen en düşük sürümü bildirir
findings.finding: Two parts of the version check can go. Two release-info sources (a release-time file or GitHub with a token and cache) is one more than needed; the GitHub path adds a secret that GitHub recommends giving an expiry, so it needs rotation. The APK hash is redundant for updates, because Android installs an update only when its signing certificate matches the installed app's.

evidence.quote: To provide additional security, we highly recommend adding an expiration to your personal access tokens.
When the system is installing an update to an app, it compares the certificate(s) in the new version with those in the existing version. The system allows the update if the certificates match.

findings.recommendation_tr: Yayın bilgisi tek yerden gelir: CI yayın sırasında küçük bir dosya yazar, sunucu yalnız onu okur. GitHub'dan anahtarla okuma yolunu kaldırırım; böylece süreli anahtarı yenileme işi de kalkar. APK özetini de çıkarırım, çünkü Android güncellemeyi zaten yalnız aynı imza anahtarıyla imzalanmış APK için kabul ediyor.

findings.plan_quote: Yalnız hata düzeltmeleri için kullanılır; Apple yeni özelliği bu yolla vermeye izin vermiyor.
findings.finding: Because the plan forbids forced updates mid-semester, it may be tempting to ship Aşama 2 or 3 code dormant in an early binary and switch it on later from the server or by OTA. Apple forbids both: hidden or dormant features are banned (2.3.1(a)), and DPLA 3.3.1(C) bans unlocking additional functionality outside the App Store or TestFlight. The plan's OTA rule should state this explicitly.

evidence.quote: Don't include any hidden, dormant, or undocumented features in your app; your app's functionality should be clear to end users and App Review.
an Application may not provide, unlock or enable additional features or functionality through distribution mechanisms other than the App Store, Custom App Distribution or TestFlight.

findings.recommendation_tr: Aşama 2 ve 3'ün kodunu ilk sürüme gizli koyup sonradan sunucudan ya da uzaktan güncellemeyle açmam. Apple hem gizli ve uyuyan özelliği hem de mağaza dışından özellik açmayı yasaklıyor. Bu aşamalar incelemeden geçen yeni sürümle gelir.

findings.plan_quote: Apple geliştirici hesabı yılda 99 USD; bireysel hesaba ücret muafiyeti yok.
findings.finding: A lapsed membership makes the app impossible to download, so new students cannot install it, and it blocks store updates. A one-person project should not depend on remembering a yearly payment.

evidence.quote: If your Apple Developer Program membership expires, your apps will no longer be available for download and you won't be able to submit new apps or updates or access Certificates, Identifiers & Profiles.

findings.recommendation_tr: Apple üyeliğinde otomatik yenilemeyi açarım. Üyelik düşerse uygulama yeni öğrencilere indirilemez ve mağazaya güncelleme gönderemem; kurulu uygulamalar çalışmaya devam eder.

compactness_notes:
My recommendations change the moving-part count by about zero. One part is added: an S3-compatible bucket for xprem. It fixes a real gap, because xprem's own docs say local disk is not for production, and MinIO was archived in April 2026. Two parts are removed: the GitHub token read path for release info, and the APK hash field with its client-side hashing step. Every other recommendation is a rule, not a tool.

xprem is still the best fit:
- It is the only self-hosted option that keeps Expo's own client (expo-updates, about 4.85M weekly downloads) and gives signing, percentage rollouts and rollback under MIT.
- Hosted EAS Update would remove the container, but code signing needs the Production plan at 199 USD a month (50K MAU included). The free plan covers 1K MAU and has no signing.
- hot-updater replaces expo-updates with its own native module. It has one dominant maintainer in a user-owned repo and 1.0 is still in release candidates.
- Expo's custom-expo-updates-server says it is a demo, 'not guaranteed to be complete, stable, or performant enough'.
- Writing the protocol into Fastify would rebuild rollouts, rollback and signing by hand.
- Stateless xprem drops the database, but it loses rollouts and brings back an Expo token dependency.

The compact setup is xprem control-plane in a separate database on the existing PostgreSQL server, with in-memory cache (no Redis), no CDN, the dashboard reached only through an SSH tunnel, and a pinned image tag. OTA earns its place mainly for the Android GitHub path (about 77% of phones), where a new APK needs manual installs. AltStore-style sideloading, the Enterprise program and Apple School Manager custom apps are rightly left out.
open_questions: Line 84 is in another slice: it blocks account deletion while unsent records exist. App Review 5.1.1(v) requires in-app deletion but accepts a delay if the user is told ('If the deletion request will take additional time to complete, let them know', https://developer.apple.com/support/offering-account-deletion-in-your-app/). Should the rule say 'the request is accepted and completed after pending records are sent', so review does not fail on an offline phone?

Who owns the Apple account: the owner's individual account, or an İÜ organization account (AUZEF already publishes on the App Store)? This decides fee-waiver eligibility and the name and logo permission. Because of the keychain risk on transfer, it has to be settled before the first TestFlight build.

xprem's docs describe loading locally generated keys only as a migration from stateless mode or v2. It is not documented whether a fresh control-plane server takes a pre-generated key pair on first boot; this needs confirming before the first build.
xprem's docs do not state which PostgreSQL versions are supported, so compatibility with PostgreSQL 18 is unverified.
Which S3-compatible bucket to use depends on the hosting provider, and the plan does not name one.
